caveats: In-process numbers come from :timer.tc inside the same dev-mode BEAM (mix run, not a release) that runs the benchmark; the first call of each API includes module loading.

Step 1 CLI timings include BEAM boot, Mix project loading and HarnessForge application start (workspace lock, SQLite open/migrations, Oban, endpoint without HTTP listener); they were spawned as nested OS processes from this script and measured with /usr/bin/time -p.
Step 1 uses a sibling workspace (<scratch>/bench-ws-cli) because the benchmark process owns <scratch>/bench-ws and a workspace admits one owning OS process.

Other processes on the machine (for this run: a second HarnessForge portal from a concurrent agent on PORT 8866 with its own workspace) add light background load; no isolation or CPU pinning was applied.
Repeated builds re-verify an existing content-addressed artifact instead of writing it; only the first build per runtime includes publication to disk.
Compiler sizes above the v1alpha1 schema limit for spec.rules are not representable; see steps.6_compiler.size_note.
Evidence.search/1 latency includes loading every matching source with its revision body (up to 50 per query).
Decisions and the first demo load cannot be repeated on the same workspace, so they are single measurements.

10_footprint.note: Measured after step 9; MB are decimal megabytes (1e6 bytes); RSS from ps -o rss= (KiB).

1_beam_boot.note: Measured from the shell with /usr/bin/time -p (real seconds) in a nested OS process; first invocation after creating the sibling workspace is a warm-up (migrations) and is reported separately. mix run -e :ok and bin/harnessforge status both boot the BEAM, load the Mix project and start the application; mix run --no-start -e :ok isolates BEAM + Mix boot.

3_decisions.note: Each decision is append-only and can run only once per claim revision, so no repetition is possible; the deliberately malicious third demo claim is never decided.

4_build.note: The first build of each runtime compiles, verifies and publishes the content-addressed artifact to disk; repeated builds (step 5) find the existing digest and re-verify it instead of writing.

6_compiler.method: Rules replicate the first real rule of the opencode artifact spec with unique synthetic UUIDs and statements; evidence citations, revision hash and goal reference are kept so semantic checks (byte ranges, goal ids, duplicate ids) pass.
6_compiler.size_note: 1000 rules exceeds the v1alpha1 schema limit (spec.rules maxItems = 500); the largest allowed size 500 was used instead.

8_import.note: sync of a local connection re-reads every file inside one SQLite transaction (bodies + FTS5 index rows); MB are decimal megabytes (1e6 bytes). Re-syncs of the unchanged corpus are reported separately.

9_search.note: Evidence.search/1 runs an FTS5 MATCH (literal tokens, LIMIT 50) and then loads every hit as a source DTO including its current revision body; latency therefore includes result materialisation, not only the index lookup.
